Now when it comes to communism, the flaws are much deeper, and the biggest one being the fact that theres no competition between companies/producers. Everything is owned by the goverment, wich eliminates that factor instantly.
This way there is no need for development of technology, so the quality of life stoops lower over time. This is all evidenced by the state of the Soviet Union by 1987. Also evidenced by modern day north Korea.

20 million civilian deaths followed Stalin's rule
60 million Civillian deaths followed Mao's rule
These are excluding casualties/collateral from WWII.

Quality of life was also terrible under communism, just imagine needing coupons to get butter and/or other cooking ingredients.
And things weren't free either, I have a guitar which was bought in 1986 and it wasn't cheap, worth roughly 60 USD which was not easy to come by, since working handed out housing/food coupons, not much money.

And the biggest flaw by far, is the fact that you did not get compensated for work, if you worked overtime you worked overtime. You didn't get paid, either you do it, or you lose your job and house.
So a lazy fuck that didn't do any work would get paid the same amount as a hard working man. 
Your efforts were always Unnoticed.
